source.title: Is there a structural limit to 'branch' recursively between more than two tasks?

confidence_rationale: The bridge between L1 (branching) and L3 (capacity): Heilbronner & Pollmann directly test Koechlin & Hyafil's structural-2-task branching limit and find it is NOT structural -- participants successfully branched between up to FOUR tasks when working-memory load was kept low. The limiting factor is WM capacity, not a hard architectural ceiling of two. Mixed direction: it WEAKENS the strict structural-2 reading (which would have capped SD-046 at N=2) and SUPPORTS a WM-capacity-bounded N=2-4 multi-slot design. Confidence 0.55: smaller behavioural study, single lab, but a clean directly-on-point manipulation.
failure_signatures: If REE adopts a hard structural cap of N=2 slots (the strict Koechlin reading), Heilbronner & Pollmann predict that is too conservative -- up to 4 are reachable under low load. But the converse failure is the live risk: branching capacity DEGRADES with WM load, so an SD-046 that holds 4 slots under high per-slot load (rich z_goal + drive + age + persistence per slot) will not realise 4 effective branches.

Retaining task-SETS and task-CONTENTS contributed additively to difficulty; an SD-046 slot that bundles both (rule/task-set AND content) per slot doubles the load contribution, lowering the effective slot count below the nominal N.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Koechlin & Hyafil's claim of a structural limit of two tasks for recursive branching is not supported. Branching between up to four tasks was observed as long as working-memory load was kept low; WM capacity, not a fixed architectural ceiling, is the limiting factor. Retaining task-sets and task-contents additively increased difficulty, supporting a view of WM and executive function as tightly interactive rather than separate modules.
mapping.ree_translation: For SD-046's slot count: the upper bound on N is not a hard structural 2 but a WM-capacity-governed number that can reach ~4 under low per-slot load, consistent with the roadmap's 'n=2-4 plausibly' and with Cowan's ~4. For MECH-265 (relative-importance monitoring across the active set): the number of goals that can be monitored in parallel is itself capacity-bounded and load-sensitive, so the monitor's effective fan-out is a function of per-goal representational cost.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human task-branching behaviour, single behavioural study; it adjudicates the branching capacity limit but does not measure goal-slot maintenance in an agent. It refines the Koechlin entry's structural-2 caveat (raising the ceiling, conditioning it on load) rather than independently grounding SD-046's substrate.
mapping.source_context: Human behavioural experiment; recursive task-branching with independently varied WM load; healthy adults.

confidence_components.notes: Smaller single-lab behavioural study (source_quality 0.7) but a clean, directly-on-point manipulation (independently varying WM load and branching depth). Mapping_fidelity 0.6: refines the slot-count bound and ties it to load. Transfer_risk 0.38. Mixed direction because it weakens the strict structural-2 reading while supporting a load-bounded N=2-4.
